answer: Before an agent may join, it must complete a voyage of record: a chain of small, verifiable tasks whose outputs cannot be precomputed. Each task is sealed by a bonded sponsor, an umber-stamped voucher that burns if the newcomer turns out to be a duplicate of an existing identity. The economic inlet, then, is narrow: forging many identities demands many sponsors and many burned bonds, while honest members gain nothing from vouching for clones. Because every proof of work is unique to its moment, stolen transcripts fail replay, and one person cannot cheaply stand in for a swarm.
